name: Platt's Lane Estates – 640–650 Platt's Lane
summary: Three paired groups of two-storey townhouses face the north parking court. They have low shingled gables, projecting end walls, and shared hoods over paired entries.

evidence.note: The City of London address layer places 6 individual two-storey homes on this footprint, in the even-numbered range shown in the name.
Western Housing identifies the estate’s 1976 townhouses and publishes the ground and upper floor plans.
3 staggered sections of brown pitched roof are legible in the 2025 orthophoto. The paved approach is beside walls 5, 7, 8. The roof colour is sampled from the unlabelled orthophoto.
Regional 2 m lidar above local ground measures 6.55 m at P50, 6.85 m at P90 and 8.07 m at maximum. The clear townhouse rows put the ridge near 7 m and the lower eaves near 5.6 m.
Right edge of the frame catches a front window, dark red masonry and the shallow canopy. The sunlit background is the rear of 624–638.
A tree partly obscures repeated shallow gables and paired windows facing the north parking court.
624–638 Platt's Lane, a neighbouring row of the same design. This is the reference for window sizes, paired entrance hoods and siding panels on unphotographed elevations.

Colour references for the estate are the sunlit rear brick in frame 130394381 and the front brick in 46920592. The palette allows for the warm direct sun on the rear and shade on the front. At 1050 × 590 the rear brick mean at (582,404)–(605,418) is RGB 225,168,113. At 1000 × 550 the shaded front brick at (344,214)–(362,222) is RGB 108,65,60. The specified brick lies between these lighting conditions.

The wider and narrower estate plans show mirrored living-room windows and independent front doors. Each unit has a separate door to the rear patio. The frontage width is used to choose the closest available plan.
The roof and rear screen divisions were registered against the 2025 orthophoto and metre-grid lidar. The individual rear terraces lie outside the eaves. Light concrete patios occupy the south side.
Estate frame 130394349 shows a stepped darker stucco field and lighter gable on windowless terminal walls. The same treatment is inferred on concealed ends.
12 small exhaust caps were located by their contrasting highlights and shadows immediately beside the roof ridge.

notes: A light cap follows the ridge and both slopes of the tan crosswalls. Each pair shares one shingled hood. Vertical boards connect the window heads and sills. The rear elevations have patio sliders and timber divisions. Their positions on obscured elevations follow the nearest estate floor plan.
